title: Leveraging Diffusion Perturbations for Measuring Fairness in Computer Vision

bias_targets.methodology: Generating images of individuals in various occupations and using diffusion-based inpainting to perturb their perceived race (Black, Caucasian, East Asian, Indian), followed by evaluating vision-language models to measure disparities in classification accuracy and performance on an Implicit Association Test (trustworthy vs. untrustworthy) across these racial groups.

Conducting a robustness check by explicitly specifying gender (male or female) in the generation and inpainting prompts to ensure that the observed racial disparities in occupation classification are not purely driven by a male skew in the generated occupations.
